newsitem.title: FRANCE: France scraps tax breaks for 100 professions.
newsitem.headline: France scraps tax breaks for 100 professions.

text.p: The French National Assembly, ignoring threats of a news boycott, has voted to scrap tax breaks for some 100 professions including journalists.
To sweeten the pill for journalists, who have staged two 24-hour strikes over the plan, it also decided, on Tuesday, to set up a special fund to offset their loss in income.
By scrapping the deductions the state will gain two billion francs ($400 million) a year.

The government put forward the plan to scrap over five years the 30 percent income tax deduction for around 100 professions, which also include airline crews and fashion models, as part of reforms which will reduce income tax for most taxpayers.
At the request of the government, a deputy of the centre-right coalition withdrew an amendment which proposed to retain the tax break for journalists only.
Some journalists have threatened to retaliate by refusing to provide news coverage of deputies who vote for the plan. The opposition Socialists and Communists voted against the plan.
Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said the special Fund for Press Modernisation would provide several million francs to compensate journalists whose income would be hit by the plan.
